areas.rotation_note_ja: Almaty's east-west avenues (Abai, Satbayev, Timiryazev, Tole Bi) bear about N84E (principal axis +5 to +6 deg counter-clockwise from east in the fetched OSM geometry); with the app's rotation (x=u*cos-v*sin, y down) a negative value tilts the grid up-right to match (derived)
areas.flood_context_ja: ThinkHazard rates river flood and urban flood for Almaty City area as Very low, but the real water hazard is mudflow (sel): the valleys of the Kishi (Malaya) and Ulken (Bolshaya) Almatinka rivers that cross the city saw five catastrophic debris flows in the 20th century, the worst in 1921 when about 10 million m3 of mud and rock at 900 m3/s killed about 500 of the then 45,000 inhabitants and destroyed much of the city (Wikipedia, Medeu Dam). The Medeu mudflow-control dam, created by blasting on 21 October 1966, stopped the 15 July 1973 flow that would otherwise have reached the city; 8 million m3 of sediment was trapped and the dam was later raised (reservoir capacity about 12.6 million m3 after 1980, search_snippet). Glacial-lake outbursts remain a live threat: on 23 July 2015 an outburst into the Kargalinka river sent a mudflow through Chapaevo, Kargaly and Kamenka in Nauryzbay district (western outskirts), with about 900 evacuated, five injured and a city state of emergency (ECHO Daily Flash via ReliefWeb). Within this frame the channelized Kishi Almaty (east of Dostyk), the Esentai/Vesnovka (past Esentai Tower) and the Ulken Almaty (western edge) are the corridors to avoid when KazSelezaschita or the Almaty DChS issue mudflow warnings (June-August).
areas.earthquake_context_ja: ThinkHazard rates earthquake hazard High for Almaty City area (page_read). The city (then Verny) was destroyed by the 1887 earthquake (about M7.3, intensity IX in Verny, at least 330 dead, 1,798 brick houses destroyed) and again on 3 January 1911 by the M8.0 Kemin (Kebin) earthquake 37 km to the south (USGS iscgem16958130; 452 killed, more than 770 brick buildings collapsed). USGS lists 23 M5+ events within 150 km since 1950 (the latest in 2014); the M7.0 Wushi (Uqturpan) earthquake of 22 January 2024, about 270 km away, produced 235 USGS 'Did You Feel It' reports from Almaty with community intensity 4.6 and a PAGER yellow fatality / red economic alert (USGS us7000lsze via the project's USGS dataset), and residents left high-rise apartments into the winter night (widely reported; unverified here). The design intensity is MSK-64 9 for most of the city; the Institute of Seismology names the zones north of Raiymbek Avenue with shallow groundwater and soft soils as the most unfavorable (up to 10), while the southern districts stand on coarser alluvial fans (search_snippet via Tengrinews). For a 36-storey tower this means long elevator outages, facade glass and partition damage, stairway evacuation of 14 office floors, and after-shock waiting in nearby open spaces (Esentai Park, KazNU campus, Botanical Garden). Landslide susceptibility is Medium (ThinkHazard) and concentrates on the Gorny Gigant / Kok Tobe slopes.
areas.heat_cold_haze_context_ja: Continental climate (Dfa) at 870 m: Open-Meteo daily data for 16 Aug - 22 Nov 2026 show a maximum of 36.8 C and a minimum of -5.9 C already in November (page_read); ThinkHazard rates extreme heat Medium and wildfire High. Winter smog is structural: coal and vehicle emissions trapped by temperature inversions in the heating season put Almaty among the world's most polluted major cities on single days (6th on 8 Jan 2026 and 2nd on 16 Sep 2025 in IQAir rankings; 2024 annual PM2.5 average 20.3 ug/m3), so N95/FFP2 masks and air purifiers belong in the office and home stock (search_snippet). Heavy snow and black ice on the sloping avenues (Al-Farabi, Dostyk) regularly disrupt commuting between the Esentai office and the Samal / Koktem housing (unverified, general knowledge).
areas.zone_src_ja: Demo zones assumed from published history and terrain logic: mudflow corridors drawn as +/-120-220 m buffers along the fetched OSM channels of the Kishi Almaty, Esentai and Ulken Almaty rivers (Medeu Dam and Esentai River Wikipedia pages; ECHO 2015 flash); seismic bands from the Institute of Seismology statements (MSK-64 9 city-wide, 9-10 north of Raiymbek; Tengrinews, search_snippet) and ThinkHazard 'High'; urban-flood patches are assumptions (ThinkHazard: Very low). No official microzonation or sel-hazard polygons were fetched.

areas.area_ja: Atyrau centre - both banks of the Zhaiyk (Satpayev / Azattyq / Baimukhanov)
areas.flood_context_ja: Atyrau lies about 20 m below sea level on the flat Zhaiyk (Ural) delta plain, split by the river into a European (west) and an Asian (east) bank, and ThinkHazard rates both river flood and urban flood hazard High for the Atyrau city area. The Ural is 60-70% snowmelt-fed and carries about 65% of its annual flow in the spring flood (March-April near the mouth): in the record 2024 flood the Atyrau gauge rose past its 550 cm critical mark to 553 cm in mid-May, more than 520 km of earth dikes were raised in the region, garden-plot (dacha) societies and houses in the floodplain were pre-emptively evacuated, a dike at Sokolok near the city was reported breached around 24 May (143 evacuees sheltered in a school) and the city's power plants were fenced against the water, while the city core behind the embankments stayed dry. Kazhydromet expected the crest at Uralsk (critical level 850 cm) on 18-20 April, whereas Atyrau's peak came only in mid-May (13 May: 'peak expected in 4-5 days'), so river floods here are forecastable weeks ahead; in 2024 the inflow also lifted the Caspian level near Atyrau by 119 cm (Ministry of Water Resources via bizmedia.kz). Spring thaw and rain additionally pond in low-lying panel-housing microdistricts with limited storm drainage (Avangard, Zhilgorodok, station area) - an assumption consistent with the urban-flood rating.
areas.earthquake_context_ja: ThinkHazard rates earthquake hazard Very low for the Atyrau city area, and the USGS catalog holds no M5+ event within 150 km since 1950; the largest nearby events are M4.5 (2023-04-25, ~250 km S near Shetpe) and M4.5 (2026-09-17, ~160 km SE near Karaton). A cluster of 11 M4.0-4.5 events since 2020 lies 130-160 km south-east around Karaton and the Tengiz field (USGS); whether it is induced by field operations is not established here (assumption). Soviet-era panel and brick housing predates seismic design, so the plausible risk is non-structural damage and panic at low intensities; mudflow/debris flow is not relevant on the flat delta.
areas.heat_cold_context_ja: Extreme heat is rated Medium by ThinkHazard: the record high is 44.6 C (August), July mean daily maximum 33.7 C, and Open-Meteo shows 37.1 C as recently as 2026-08-25 (Wikipedia climate table 1991-2020; Open-Meteo). Winters are severe for a city at sea level - record low -37.9 C (January), January mean -6.4 C with steppe winds and ice on the Zhaiyk - so power or heating outages in winter are a life-safety issue for staff housing. Water scarcity and wildfire (steppe and reed fires in the delta) are rated High, and the city has chronic hydrogen-sulfide air-pollution episodes from the oil and gas industry (Wikipedia); Caspian coastal flood is 'No data' in ThinkHazard and affects the delta villages (Damba, 46.96 N) rather than the city (assumption).
areas.zone_src_ja: Assumed polygons: Zhaiyk floodplain strips from the OSM river geometry (Nominatim relation 214415) within about 0.7 km of the channel; 2024 reports (gauge 553 cm vs 550 cm critical; dikes held in the core; floodplain dacha societies and houses evacuated; Sokolok dike breach NE of the city; power plant fenced); low-lying microdistricts for urban ponding; ThinkHazard river/urban flood High. No published inundation map for Atyrau city was accessible (none on ReliefWeb/HDX; Copernicus/UNOSAT not activated for Atyrau).

RSCEMP, AKFA Medline, Tashkent International Clinic/School, the MES HQ, the MoD Central Military Hospital, the US Embassy and the TV tower lie outside the frame; they are kept in pois (with true coordinates) or in _meta.facts so that distance tables still work. Babur Street and the Chilanzar end of Bunyodkor Avenue are clipped at the frame edge
areas.flood_context_ja: ThinkHazard rates river flood and urban flood Low for Tashkent city (report 39698, page_read), while the surrounding Tashkent Region is High for both (report 3295): the city sits on the Chirchik alluvial fan at about 455 m, drained by the Soviet-era canal network (Bozsu, Anhor, Salar, Oqtepa; OSM relations via Nominatim) fed from the Chirchik below the Charvak reservoir, and the river itself passes 10 km south-east of the centre. No river flood has reached the central districts in the modern record; the regional reference event is the May 2020 Sardoba reservoir failure in neighbouring Sirdaryo Region (about 70,000 evacuated; ECHO via ReliefWeb). The practical water hazard in the centre is pluvial: spring thunderstorms (March-June) flood underpasses, basements and the low Mirabad / railway-station ground for hours (assumption; no public pluvial map was found). Mudflow and debris-flow corridors do not reach the city frame - they lie in the Bostanliq, Parkent and Akhangaran foothills 40-70 km to the north-east and east (Tashkent Region landslide High).
areas.earthquake_context_ja: ThinkHazard rates earthquake High for Tashkent city (page_read). At 05:23 on 26 April 1966 a shallow M5.2 earthquake (USGS ISC-GEM M5.3, 10 km, 41.345N 69.184E; Wikipedia: 3-8 km deep with the epicentre in the centre) destroyed most of the old adobe city, left 200,000-300,000 of about 1.5 million residents homeless and killed between 15 and 200; the Monument of Courage on Sharof Rashidov Street marks the epicentral zone and the city was rebuilt with wide boulevards and panel housing over three and a half years (Wikipedia; UNDP/ReliefWeb 2016). USGS lists M5.2 in 1970 (5 km SSE of the city) and M5.1 in 1980 (4 km W) as well as the 1959 Gazalkent M6.0 (62 km NE) and the 1946 Chatkal M7.5 (190 km) as regional references (page_read, sibling usgs.json). Tashkent is in zone 8-9 (MSK-64) of the national seismic building code on up to 15 m of loess and alluvium that amplify shaking (search_snippet; Wikipedia for the deposits); self-built mahalla houses remain the most vulnerable stock (UNDP/ReliefWeb 2014). For a high-rise office the governing issues are elevator entrapment, facade and glass fall, gas shut-off and assembly in open parks rather than collapse.
areas.heat_cold_haze_context_ja: Hot-summer continental climate at 455 m: July mean 28.3 C with an all-time record of 44.6 C (18 July 1997, Wikipedia) and 44.3 C on 19 July 2026 (kun.uz, search_snippet); Open-Meteo daily data for 16 August - 22 November 2026 near the city show a maximum of 37.7 C (19 August), 12 days at or above 35 C and a minimum of 0.6 C (page_read); ThinkHazard rates extreme heat Medium and water scarcity Medium. Winters are cold (January mean 2.3 C, record low -29.5 C, Wikipedia): the January 2023 cold wave (about -20 C) coincided with the halt of Turkmen gas imports and power rationing, leaving apartment blocks unheated and prompting protests and the mayor's dismissal (bne IntelliNews, search_snippet). Air quality: the 4 November 2021 dust storm (dust 30 times the limit, about 4,000 ambulance calls; UNCCD, search_snippet) and winter inversion smog recur; ThinkHazard wildfire High refers to steppe and grass fires outside the built-up area.
areas.zone_src_ja: Demo zones are assumptions: canal corridors drawn as +/-130 m buffers along the fetched OSM geometry of the Anhor and Salar canals (ThinkHazard river/urban flood Low, so illustrative only); pluvial ponding polygons at known low spots and underpasses (no public pluvial map); seismic bands from the 1966 epicentral / old-city damage area (Wikipedia, UNDP via ReliefWeb) and the national seismic zoning 8-9 MSK (search_snippet), plus a high-rise cluster band around Tashkent City.

areas.rotation_note_ja: Bishkek's Soviet grid is almost cardinal: the fetched OSM geometry of Chuy Avenue bears 1.5 deg south of east and Chyngyz Aytmatov (Manas) Avenue 2.3 deg east of north, i.e. about 2 deg clockwise; with the app's rotation convention (x=u*cos-v*sin, y down; the Almaty frame used -6 for a 5-6 deg counter-clockwise tilt) a small positive value matches (derived)
areas.flood_context_ja: River flood is rated Low for Chuy Region and the Bishkek city division has no ThinkHazard data at all (page_read), but the city has three live water hazards. (1) Mudflow and ice jams on the Ala-Archa, which enters the frame from the south at Ataturk Park, runs diagonally north-west past Akhunbaev/Maldybaev streets and then north along the former Molodaya Gvardiya boulevard 1 km west of the office: on 16 December 2023 an avalanche-fed frazil-ice (shuga) jam pushed the river out of its channel and flooded Akhunbaev and Maldybaev streets, and on 17 July 2024 the city declared a special readiness regime for a possible mudflow from the Ala-Archa gorge (economist.kg, kaktus.media; search_snippet). The river is small (mean 4.2 m3/s, max 50 m3/s; Wikipedia) but channelized and hemmed in by housing, and MES clears the channel every spring and autumn. (2) The Alamudun (Alamedin) along the eastern edge of the frame (mean 6.4 m3/s, max 300 m3/s) needs winter ice-clearing (11 km cleared in 2024-25; Wikipedia third_party). (3) The Great Chuy Canal (BChK, 43-55 m3/s at its head) crosses the north of the frame from east to west 1 km north of Jibek Jolu; it is an unlined earth canal built 1941-58 with buildings inside its former mudflow channels (CABAR, search_snippet), so a breach or blocked culvert floods the flat northern districts. Short, intense summer storms (May-July) also pond water in the low northern blocks and at underpasses (ThinkHazard: urban flood High nationally, Low for Chuy; assumption for the city).
areas.earthquake_context_ja: ThinkHazard rates earthquake hazard High for Chuy Region and nationally (page_read). Bishkek sits on the alluvial fans of the northern Kyrgyz Ala-Too immediately north of the Issyk-Ata marginal fault, whose nearest segment runs along the Chon-Aryk and Pospeldek foothills 5-8 km south of this frame (kaktus.media, search_snippet). The national zoning places the city in the 9-point (MSK-64) zone and Gosstroy states that modern high-rises are designed for intensity 9 (24.kg, search_snippet; design intensity itself unverified); a 2019 SNiP re-rated the 700 m fault-adjacent zone from 9 to 8 points while banning construction in two 250 m strips. Published scenarios for a Mw 7.5 Issyk-Ata rupture give 7,900 +/- 2,600 completely damaged buildings and 2,400 +/- 1,500 deaths (Amey and Elliott 2023), with site effects adding up to 2 intensity units in the flat, water-saturated north of the city (Bindi et al. 2011; search_snippet). History: 1885 Belovodsk (about 9 points, 45 km west), 1887 Verny (9-10), 1911 Kemin M8.0 (180 km east, destroyed Almaty and damaged Pishpek), 1938 Kemin-Chu M7.0 (110 km east) and 1992 Suusamyr M7.3 (116 km south-west); USGS lists 18 M5+ events within 150 km since 1950, the latest M5.0 on 12 August 2026 (page_read). The M7.0 Wushi earthquake of 22 January 2024 produced 124 USGS felt reports from Bishkek (intensity 3.8) and sent residents into the streets. Soviet 1960s-80s panel and brick housing (Vostok-5, microdistricts) and the fast-built high-rises of the southern Kosmos/Asanbai belt are the vulnerability concern; ThinkHazard landslide is High for the region but slope failure matters only on the southern foothills, outside this frame.
areas.heat_cold_haze_context_ja: Continental climate at 760-800 m: Open-Meteo daily data for 16 Aug - 22 Nov 2026 show 35.7 C and -3.4 C (page_read); summer peaks reach 39-42 C (country file) and ThinkHazard rates extreme heat Medium. Winter is the critical season: in December 2012 Bishkek declared a state of emergency during the coldest spell in 76 years (-30 to -35 C, 16 dead nationally; ReliefWeb/IFRC page_read), and the single district-heating source, the Soviet-era Bishkek CHP (TETs) on Chuy Avenue 206 just east of the frame, failed in January 2018 (three days without heat at -25 C) and again on 2 February 2024 when a boiler exploded (five injured, heating and hot water limited for days, schools online; search_snippet). Power rationing under the 2023-2026 energy emergency compounds this. Heating-season smog from coal stoves and inversions puts Bishkek among the world's most polluted cities on winter days (IQAir: most polluted major city on 16 March 2026, AQI 160; 2024 annual PM2.5 21.2 ug/m3; search_snippet), so FFP2 masks, purifiers and a heating fallback (electric heaters, generator fuel) belong in the office and home stock.
areas.zone_src_ja: Demo zones are assumptions drawn from fetched geometry and published events: mudflow/ice-jam corridors are +/-200 m buffers along the OSM channel of the Ala-Archa and +/-150 m along the Alamudun (Nominatim relations 7062681 and 19640713, page_read), a +/-80 m breach strip along the Great Chuy Canal (relation 10674491); the urban-flood patches mark the Akhunbaev/Maldybaev area flooded on 16 December 2023 (search_snippet) and the flat northern blocks (assumed); seismic bands use the 9-point national zone (unverified), the +2 intensity site-amplification finding for the north of the city (Bindi et al., search_snippet) and the fault proximity of the southern belt. No official microzonation or mudflow hazard polygons were fetched.

areas.area_ja: Central Dushanbe (Rudaki Avenue - Ismoili Somoni Avenue - Varzob river; Ismoili Somoni, Shohmansur, Sino and Firdavsi districts)
areas.rotation_note_ja: Dushanbe's east-west spines are almost exactly east-west in the fetched OSM geometry (Ismoili Somoni Avenue principal axis -6.2 deg, Nazarshoev -2.0 deg, Shohtemur +2.9 deg from east), while Rudaki Avenue runs NNW (axis -78.1 deg) as a diagonal; the grid is therefore left unrotated (derived)
areas.flood_context_ja: ThinkHazard rates river flood only Low for the Dushanbe/DRS division but urban flood and landslide High (page_read): the water hazard here is the Varzob - called Dushanbinka inside the city - a 71 km mountain torrent (basin 1,740 km2) that enters the frame from the north past the Botanical Garden, passes 350 m west of the Flagpole Park and Rudaki Park and leaves south of Saadi Sherozi Avenue, joined by the Luchob from the west (Wikipedia; OSM geometry). Rain-on-snow and glacier-melt mudflows in the Varzob gorge repeatedly damage the single water intake: in July 2004 about 400,000 residents of the capital were without clean water and 26 km of the Varzob road were destroyed (EM-DAT / IRIN, via the regional file), in May 2016 a Varzob mudslide again cut downtown water for a day (ReliefWeb), and the 1993 flood of about 1,000 m3/s destroyed bridges and intakes (JICA, search_snippet). Late-August 2023 rains killed 21 people in Vahdat, Rudaki and Varzob and damaged houses in Luchob village (Crisis24, search_snippet). Inside the frame the exposure is concentrated in the riverside strips (Sari Osiyo houses, Flagpole Park, Navruzgoh, the Firdavsi lowland) and in water-supply disruption for every office and home; spring (Mar-Jun) and Jul-Aug are the danger months.
areas.earthquake_context_ja: ThinkHazard rates earthquake hazard High (page_read) and the city sits in the 9-point zone of the Tajik MSK-64 code (SNiP RT 22-07-2018; UNDP risk profile 'high-seismicity zone, estimated 8-9' - search_snippet, official zone value unverified). The 1907 Qaratog earthquake (Mw 7.44, 99 km west, intensity IX, 12,000-15,000 dead; USGS ISC-GEM and Wikipedia) is the regional maximum; the 1949 Khait M7.5 earthquake 190 km north-east killed about 7,200, mostly in loess flowslides; and on 22 January 1989 the mb5.3 Gissar earthquake only 14 km west triggered loess flowslides that buried Sharora and killed 274 (Wikipedia). USGS lists 50 M5+ events within 150 km since 1950 and six within 50 km, the latest the M5.2 Vahdat earthquake of 10 November 2013 (20 km, 104 houses destroyed, felt strongly in the capital; Asia-Plus snippet). Wikipedia puts the maximum credible magnitude near the city at 7.5-8. A 1975 microzonation map exists and a 2021 site-amplification study shows strong soil dependence (search_snippet): the Varzob valley gravels and fill amplify, the loess hills east of Lohuti Street are prone to flowslides, and the housing stock mixes 1920s-50s adobe/brick quarters (Shohmansur), 1970s-80s panel microdistricts (Sino, Firdavsi) and new 12-25 storey towers along Rudaki Avenue. For a 20-storey office this means elevator outage, glass/facade damage, stairway evacuation from the 9th floor and assembly in Rudaki Park or the Flagpole Park.
areas.heat_cold_haze_context_ja: Hot-summer Mediterranean climate at 820 m: record highs 44.1 C (June) and 45.0 C (August), with Open-Meteo showing 37.6 C on 19 August 2026 and 2.5 C by mid-November (page_read); ThinkHazard rates extreme heat Medium and water scarcity Medium. Summer power and water interruptions coincide with heat waves, and Afghan dust storms (June-October) and winter inversion smog degrade air quality (regional file). Winters are mild (January mean about 3 C) but the January 2008 cold wave (below -20 C, heating and electricity failures, coldest in 44 years; ReliefWeb) showed how fragile district heating and the hydropower-dependent grid are: keep heaters, fuel and water reserves for both seasons.
areas.zone_src_ja: Demo zones are assumptions drawn from published history and terrain logic: mudflow/flood corridors as +/-250 m (Varzob) and +/-150 m (Luchob) buffers along the fetched OSM channels (Wikipedia Varzob; ReliefWeb 2016; IRIN 2004; UNDP profile snippet); seismic bands from the 9-point code zone (search_snippet), soft-soil amplification along the river and loess slopes east of Lohuti Street (1989 Sharora analogy); urban-flood patches on the low Firdavsi/Shohmansur terrace and the Mehrabad confluence terrace (ThinkHazard urban flood High). No official microzonation, mudflow-hazard or flood polygons were fetched; the UNDP Dushanbe risk profile and the Geosciences 2021 paper are blocked for fetching.

areas.area_ja: Central and southern Ashgabat (Berzengi / Archabil white-marble district - Olympic complex - Parahat - old centre; Kopetdag, Berkararlyk and Bagtyyarlyk districts)
areas.rotation_note_ja: Ashgabat has two grids: the old centre (Magtymguly, Gorogly, the railway) runs WNW-ESE with a principal axis about 34 deg clockwise from east, while the post-2000 southern district (10 yyl Abadancylyk, Archabil, Chandybil) is tilted only 8-21 deg (axes computed from the fetched OSM geometry, derived). A compromise rotation of +20 deg (positive = clockwise in the app's x=u*cos-v*sin, y-down convention) makes both roughly horizontal
areas.flood_context_ja: ThinkHazard rates river flood High and urban flood Low for the Ahal division that contains Ashgabat (page_read); the city itself has no river, only the Karakum Canal 2-7 km north of this frame (between the centre and the airport) and the Ashgabat irrigation canal crossing the middle of the city. The real water hazard is flash flooding and mudflow (sil) from the Kopet Dag foothills 10-25 km to the south, plus pluvial flooding of the flat central districts: on 15-17 May 2024 three days of rain (about a quarter of the 221 mm annual average) flooded central Ashgabat, Ankara Street in Parahat was covered in water and mud, Sentinel Asia mapped floodwater from ALOS-2 imagery, and the deputy defence minister responsible for emergencies was dismissed (search_snippet: Central Asian Light, Sentinel Asia, bne/yerzemin). A 52-km complex of mudflow-diversion canals with 1-6 million m3 accumulators built by Vozrozhdenie on the main Kopet Dag channels (due September 2022) now intercepts debris flows south of Archabil Avenue and is credited with limiting the 2024 damage. The UNDP Ashgabat Risk Profile (June 2026) lists mudflows among the capital's key hazards and notes that most flood/mudflow risk originates outside city limits. Wikipedia's flood list names 1969, 1993, 1997 and 2024 as notable flood years (search_snippet). Zones in this file are assumptions: a mudflow run-out band along the southern (upslope) edge and pluvial-flood patches around Ankara Street / Parahat and the railway underpasses.
areas.earthquake_context_ja: ThinkHazard rates earthquake hazard High (Ahal division and Turkmenistan; page_read). Ashgabat was destroyed on the night of 5-6 October 1948 by an Ms 7.3 / Mw 7.15 earthquake with its ISC-GEM epicentre only 14 km north of the city (USGS iscgem897583 via the project's USGS dataset): two shocks in 10 seconds flattened nearly every adobe and fired-brick building, with 10,000-110,000 dead (Wikipedia, PAGER-CAT; official Soviet figure about 40,000, later USGS/press figure 110,000, EGU 2022 re-evaluation >38,000 - search_snippet). Epicentral shaking reached MSK-64 9-10 and pre-war standards were two to three intensity points too low (Science Council of Japan presentation, search_snippet). The city has been rebuilt twice since: Soviet 4-9-storey housing designed for intensity 8-9 and, since the 2000s, white-marble reinforced-concrete towers designed for the MSK-64 intensity 9 zone that covers all of Ashgabat (17WCEE paper 6f-0002; the 2001 national zoning map also puts the airport in zone 9 - search_snippet). USGS lists 19 M5+ events within 150 km since 1950; the largest in the region was the M7.2 Baharly (Germab) earthquake of 1 May 1929, 67 km west, and the latest M5+ was an M5.1 near Quchan, Iran, on 13 September 2021 (86 km). UNDP's 2018-2025 seismic project produced GIS hazard/risk platforms for Ashgabat whose results remain unpublished, and the 2026 regional project pilots a school earthquake-alert system in the city (search_snippet). For a 16-storey office tower the governing scenario is a repeat of 1948 at night: elevator and power outages, facade/glass and partition damage, stairway evacuation and assembly in the wide avenues and parks of Berzengi. Landslide hazard is Low (ThinkHazard) and limited to the foothill slopes south of the frame.
areas.heat_cold_haze_context_ja: Cold desert climate (BWk) at 250-280 m on the Kopet Dag piedmont, 25 km from the mountains and touching the Karakum desert to the north (Wikipedia). ThinkHazard rates extreme heat Medium for Ahal and High nationally, water scarcity High and wildfire High (page_read). Records: 47.2 C on 30 June 2015 (hottest June day on record; June 2015 was the hottest June since 1891 with 16 days above 40 C - phys.org, search_snippet), July record 46.8 C, 40 C already in April 2025 (April record since 1891), and February 2026 among the warmest on record; record low -24.1 C in January (Wikipedia climate table, third_party). Open-Meteo daily data for 16 Aug - 22 Nov 2026 show 41.3 C on 16 August, 20 days at or above 35 C and 4 days at or above 40 C (page_read). Dust is the main air-quality hazard: the strongest dust storm of 2023 crossed all regions on 13-14 April 2023 with dust from the Arabian Peninsula and West Asia (daryo.uz, search_snippet), and Aral Sea salt storms have reached the capital (RFE/RL). Summer heat with 45+ C days means cooling shelters, water, UPS for cooling in server rooms and protected outdoor assembly points; winter cold snaps to -20 C occur in January (record low -24.1 C). Air pollution from traffic is moderate and wildfire smoke is rare; FFP2 masks are kept mainly for dust days (assumption).
areas.zone_src_ja: Demo zones assumed from published history and terrain logic: the mudflow run-out band follows the southern (upslope) frame edge below the 2022 Vozrozhdenie diversion canals (newscentralasia / yerzemin, search_snippet); pluvial-flood patches are placed on Ankara Street / Parahat 1-4 (flooded 15-17 May 2024, Central Asian Light, search_snippet) and at the railway underpasses of the old centre (assumption); seismic bands apply the MSK-64 intensity 9 zone that covers the whole city (17WCEE 6f-0002, search_snippet), with an assumed 9-10 band over the old core north of Magtymguly Avenue where the 1948 destruction was total and groundwater is shallow. No official microzonation, mudflow or flood polygons were fetched; the UNDP 2026 risk-profile maps were not accessible.
